title: MCP 2.0 Features — Visual Guide
description: Interactive visual guide to the MCP 2026-07-28 specification: stateless core, MRTR, MCP Apps, Tasks, security, caching and migration.

sections.heading: MCP 2.0 at a glance
sections.summary: A visual map of the July 28, 2026 MCP specification—stateless by default, extensible by design.

views.title: Feature landscape
views.code:
mindmap
  root((MCP 2026-07-28))
    Stateless core
      Self-describing requests
      No session handshake
      Optional discovery
    HTTP at scale
      Header routing
      Cacheable catalogs
      Load balancing
    Agent interactions
      Multi-round-trip
      Subscriptions
    Extensions
      Tasks
      MCP Apps
      Enterprise auth
    Security
      OAuth alignment
      Issuer validation
      Client metadata

views.title: Release highlights
rows: Human and model input without open bidirectional streams
Lower overhead and stable prompt caches

sections.heading: Stateless architecture
sections.summary: Each request identifies its protocol version and capabilities so any healthy replica can serve it.

views.title: Request path
views.code:
flowchart LR
  U[AI application] --> C[MCP client]
  C -->|POST plus MCP headers| G[API gateway]
  G --> L[Load balancer]
  L --> S1[MCP server A]
  L --> S2[MCP server B]
  S1 --> D[(Data and tools)]
  S2 --> D
  C -.->|Optional discover| G

views.title: Stateless exchange
views.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as MCP Client
  participant G as Gateway
  participant S as MCP Server
  opt Capability discovery
    C->>G: server/discover
    G->>S: Discovery request
    S-->>C: Server capabilities
  end
  C->>G: POST tools/call + protocol _meta
  Note over C,G: Mcp-Method / Mcp-Name headers
  G->>S: Route by headers
  S-->>C: JSON-RPC result + server _meta

sections.heading: Multi Round-Trip Requests
sections.summary: A server can request more input and the client can resume the operation through explicit round trips.

views.title: Human in the loop
views.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant C as MCP Client
  participant S as MCP Server
  C->>S: tools/call
  S-->>C: input_required with request details
  C->>U: Request confirmation or information
  U-->>C: Provide input
  C->>S: Continue request with supplied input
  S-->>C: Completed result

views.title: Decision flow
views.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Client sends request] --> B[Server evaluates]
  B --> C{More input needed?}
  C -->|No| D[Return result]
  C -->|Yes| E[Return input_required]
  E --> F[Client obtains input]
  F --> G[Client retries with input]
  G --> B

sections.heading: Extensions: Apps, Tasks and enterprise auth
sections.summary: The core protocol stays lean while negotiated extensions add specialized capabilities.

views.title: Extension ecosystem
views.code:
mindmap
  root((MCP Extensions))
    MCP Apps
      Interactive interfaces
      Rich tool experiences
    Tasks
      Long-running operations
      Task status
      Result retrieval
    Enterprise Managed Authorization
      Organization policies
      Managed identity
    Custom extensions
      Capability negotiation
      Versioned contracts

views.title: Capability negotiation
views.code:
flowchart LR
  A[Client declares extensions] --> C[Compatible capabilities]
  B[Server declares extensions] --> C
  C --> D{Extension supported?}
  D -->|Yes| E[Enable extended workflow]
  D -->|No| F[Use core MCP behavior]

sections.heading: HTTP routing and discovery
sections.summary: Method and tool names are visible to infrastructure without parsing the JSON-RPC body.

views.title: Gateway policy
views.code:
flowchart TD
  A[HTTP POST] --> B[Read Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name]
  B --> C{Authorized route?}
  C -->|No| D[Reject request]
  C -->|Yes| E[Select backend replica]
  E --> F[Execute JSON-RPC method]
  F --> G[Return response]

views.title: Transport changes
rows: Continuously open streams for reverse calls

sections.heading: Cacheable catalogs and predictable ordering
sections.summary: Catalog results are designed for repeatability, reuse and stable model context.

views.title: Cache-aware listing
views.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant K as Cache
  participant S as MCP Server
  C->>K: Need tools/list
  alt Cached response valid
    K-->>C: Ordered tool catalog
  else Cache expired
    C->>S: tools/list
    S-->>C: Deterministic list + cache hints
    C->>K: Store until TTL
  end

views.title: Catalog lifecycle
views.code:
flowchart LR
  A[tools/list] --> B[Deterministic ordering]
  B --> C[Cache TTL hints]
  C --> D[Client cache]
  D --> E[Reduced repeated calls]
  D --> F[Stable prompt prefixes]

sections.heading: Authentication and authorization
sections.summary: The release hardens OAuth-style identity handling and shifts client onboarding toward metadata documents.

views.title: Security checkpoints
views.code:
flowchart TD
  A[MCP client] --> B[Read authorization server metadata]
  B --> C[Validate issuer identity]
  C --> D[Use client metadata document]
  D --> E[OAuth authorization]
  E --> F[Gateway validates credentials and scopes]
  F --> G[Authorized tool request]

views.title: Security changes
rows: Client metadata documents over dynamic registration
Method and tool headers usable in policy

sections.heading: Migration from MCP 2025 to 2026
sections.summary: Review sessions, handshake, metadata, reverse calls and SDK compatibility before upgrading.

views.title: Upgrade plan
views.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Inventory clients and servers] --> B[Check SDK and protocol support]
  B --> C[Remove initialize and sessions for 2026]
  C --> D[Add protocol metadata per request]
  D --> E[Add standard HTTP routing headers]
  E --> F[Adapt reverse calls to MRTR]
  F --> G[Test extensions and authorization]
  G --> H[Run conformance and rollout]

views.title: Compatibility checklist
rows: Do not initialize on modern protocol
Use explicit tool handles if needed

sections.heading: Reference sources and roadmap
sections.summary: Official release and specification documents are the source of truth; future roadmap work is separate from shipped functionality.
